description:
openLCA LCIA Methods 2.8.2 copies most of its flows from ecoinvent and EF 3.1, and copies their errors with them. Five of those errors the other lists already correct -- in `ecoinvent-3.12-manual-fixes.json`, `ef-3.1-manual-fixes.json` and `stepwise-2006-additional-flows.json` -- and on the first full build that merged the list (20 October 2026, merge run `76b3ec8f`, #412, fixed in #386) the openLCA copies arrived uncorrected and landed where the other lists' rows were stopped from landing:

- `Stibnite` in `Resource / in ground` (3e0034cd, ecoinvent's own uuid) carries 1345-04-6, the manufactured antimony trisulfide, and joined EF's thirteen emission flows of the compound. ecoinvent's fix rewrites that number to 1317-86-8, the mineral's, in every release (#123, 0604).
- `Epoxiconazole` to agricultural soil (1afedfb8, ecoinvent's uuid) is the one of the package's six 135319-73-2 rows that ships without the synonym `BAS 480F`, and it minted a second fungicide; the other five reach EF's `Bas 480f` on the synonym. ecoinvent's fix restores the synonym on the rows that lack it (0826).
- `Chlordane, gamma-` (four rows) carries 5566-34-7, which is not a chlordane; Stepwise's additions refuse its row with the reasoning, and the package's four were published as a fifth chlordane (0786).
- `Ether, 1,2,2-trifluoroethyl trifluoromethyl-, HFE-236ea2` (four rows) carries 2356-62-9, which is HFE-227ea's number -- EF 3.1 registers `HFE-227EA` under it and `HFE-236ea2` under 84011-06-3, and Stepwise's row of this name carries 84011-06-3 -- so the rows reached `HFE-227EA` and GreenDelta's two numbers for one flow were reported as a collision eight times over.
- `Arsenic V` (fourteen rows) carries 61805-96-7, which names no arsenic compound: PubChem lists it only as a second registry number on 1,3-dimethylthiourea (CID 2723631), and Common Chemistry does not resolve it. The rows minted a second `Arsenic(5+)` beside the one EF 3.1 registers 17428-41-0, which `lcia-substance-decisions.json` already reads GreenDelta's `Arsenic V` as.

The corrections go in `openlca-2.8.2-manual-fixes.json` and the refusal in `openlca-2.8.2-additional-flows.json`, each with the evidence, so the package's copy of a row is read the way the row it was copied from is read. Written on 20 October 2026 against that build, where every claim below fails.

**The second defect: a row with no registry number under a spelling the ion naming standard already publishes.** `Vanadium V` (three rows, in ground water, long-term ground water and a river), `Lithium I` (one row, river) and `Titanium Ion` (fourteen rows, across air, soil and water) ship with no number, and each name is a synonym `domain/ion_names.py` writes on `Vanadium(5+)`, `Lithium(1+)` and `Titanium, ion` (#401). The name route found those synonyms and refused the hits, because an alternative-label hit on a substance that carries a registry number is the guard against a trade name (`Granite` reaching penoxsulam, #103), so each name minted a second substance under the same published label: two `Vanadium(5+)`, two `Lithium(1+)`, two `Titanium, ion`. The copy of `Titanium, ion` then made the standard's synonyms ambiguous and `carry_member_names` withdrew them from both, which is why 0401's claim on them failed too; and `characterise` stopped on the doubled `Vanadium(5+)` label.

A synonym the standard wrote is built from the substance's own name by rule, as the systematic names `_narrow_label_candidates` already accepts are, so it can be neither a trade name nor another substance's. The merge now accepts such a hit, in the narrowest form that answers for these rows: the row's own shipped name, not one of its synonyms, on a row that carries no registry number at all. A numbered row that finds nothing by its number is a disagreement, not missing evidence, and stays refused -- which is what kept ecoinvent's `Chromium IV` off chromium(6+) when every standard synonym was read as a preferred name (#401).

**The third group: rows the other lists' curated targets and unit rulings cover and the package's copies did not.** Six plain `Carbon dioxide` rows reached EF's carbon dioxide of unstated origin, where BAFU's unqualified rows were sent to the fossil flows and its `in air` rows to biogenic uptake (0669); the package's own methods score the five air rows as fossil and the resource row as uptake. Three kilogram `Peat` rows reached the megajoule fuel by name, one of them minting a biotic kilogram flow (0450, 0856); EF 3.1 (adapted) scores the biotic row 9.76 MJ/kg of fossil resource, so all three are the fuel, converted at the package's own factor. Sixteen `Hydrocarbons, unspecified` rows with no table and no number minted a second bucket beside EF's `Hydrocarbons (unspecified)` (0825). Fifty water rows in kilograms crossed onto cubic-metre flows or minted kilogram ones (0409); they are rewritten to cubic metres at 0.001 as BAFU's sixteen were. And three rows with no number -- `HG-02`, `Tribromomethane`, `Helium, in natural gas, in ground` -- minted substances the list has under another spelling, and now carry the number. `openlca-2.8.2-match-overrides.json` holds the targets and `openlca-2.8.2-manual-fixes.json` the numbers and units. The bare `Carbon` in the ground is kept: the Crustal Scarcity Indicator scores it, and nothing else does, so it is elemental carbon as a mineral resource, a flow new to the list (0915 is restated to AGRIBALYSE's rows).

**On a build without the list.** Every claim in this file names a row of `openlca-2.8.2`, so on a build that does not merge that list -- the default five-list build among them -- it reads `unresolved`, which here means only that the list is not there; decided on 20 October 2026 to leave it so rather than add a status for it.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Stibnite` reaches the mineral, not EF's antimony trisulfide
expectations.comment: On the build of 20 October 2026 it reached `Antimony Trisulfide` by 1345-04-6. `basis: cas`, because the fix rewrites the number and the row should reach the mineral by it, as ecoinvent's and BAFU's rows do.

expectations.title: All 26 openLCA epoxiconazole rows reach EF's fungicide
expectations.comment: 20 rows carry 106325-08-0 and reach it by number; six carry ecoinvent's 135319-73-2, and five of those reach it on the synonym `BAS 480F`. On the build of 20 October 2026 the sixth, to agricultural soil, minted a second `Epoxiconazole`.

expectations.title: The agricultural-soil row that ships without the synonym reaches the same substance
expectations.comment: `basis: label`: the fix supplies the synonym rather than a number, and the row should reach the substance the way its five siblings do.

expectations.title: openLCA's four `Chlordane, gamma-` rows are refused, as Stepwise's is
expectations.comment: Four rows on the build of 20 October 2026, published as a fifth chlordane under 5566-34-7. A refused row is not in `merge_outcomes` at all, which is what a count of zero says; 0786 keeps the claim that no substance is published under the number. The subject is spelled as the merge table writes the name; the package writes `Chlordane, gamma-`.

expectations.title: The rows named for HFE-236ea2 reach HFE-236ea2
expectations.comment: On the build of 20 October 2026 all four reached `HFE-227EA` by 2356-62-9, the number the package writes on them. Stepwise's row of the same name carries 84011-06-3 and reaches HFE-236ea2. `basis: cas+label`: EF 3.1 registers both `HFE-236ea2` and `HFE-236fa` under 84011-06-3, so the number reaches two substances and the row's own name settles which, which is the number-then-name rule of #146. Measured on the build of 20 October 2026 with the fix (merge run `0c16f168`).

expectations.title: openLCA's fourteen `Arsenic V` rows reach EF's arsenic(5+)
expectations.comment: On the build of 20 October 2026 they minted a second `Arsenic(5+)`, because 61805-96-7 reaches nothing and `Arsenic V` is an alternative label on a substance that carries a number, which the name route refuses.

expectations.title: One substance is registered 17428-41-0
expectations.comment: Two on the build of 20 October 2026: EF's, and the copy the fourteen rows minted, which enrichment then registered under the same number.

expectations.title: openLCA's 29 `Vanadium V` rows all reach a flow, and the three numberless ones reach `Vanadium(5+)`
expectations.comment:
29 rows: twelve carry 22537-31-1 and reach `Vanadium(5+)` by number; fourteen carry 7440-62-2, the element's number, and reach `Vanadium` by it -- the package writes the element's number on many of its ion names (#380), and a number is a ruling's question, not this rule's; the three in ground water, long-term ground water and a river (a3178646, c2e2b45b, 7b8e28ba) carry none, and on the build of 20 October 2026 minted a third substance, a second `Vanadium(5+)`, on which `characterise` then stopped. `substance_count` at most 2: the element and the ion, and a third is the defect coming back.

Restated 23 October 2026: a resource in the ground is now read as its element (`+ground-resource-is-element`), so the openLCA ground-resource rows of this name no longer reach the ion, and their flows in `Resource → Ground` are gone. The build records those two rows under the element's name, `Vanadium`, so the name selects 27 of the 29.

expectations.title: The river row reaches vanadium(5+) by its name, and the merge says so
expectations.comment: `basis: label`: the number is absent and the name is what reached the substance.

expectations.title: One substance is registered 22537-31-1
expectations.comment: Two on the build of 20 October 2026, both labelled `Vanadium(5+)`.

expectations.title: openLCA's numberless `Lithium I` row reaches `Lithium(1+)`
expectations.comment: The one `Lithium I` row of sixteen that ships with no number; it minted a second `Lithium(1+)` on the build of 20 October 2026.

expectations.title: One substance is registered 17341-24-1
expectations.comment: Two on the build of 20 October 2026.

expectations.title: openLCA's 26 `Titanium Ion` rows reach two substances, the element and the ion, and the fourteen numberless ones reach the ion
expectations.comment:
26 rows: nine carry titanium's own number 7440-32-6 and reach the element, as ecoinvent's rows of that number do (#380); two carry 22541-75-9 and reach `Titanium, ion` by it, and one spelled `Titanium, Ion` reaches it by the label; the fourteen with no number minted a second `Titanium, ion` on the build of 20 October 2026, a third substance. `substance_count` at most 2, so a third target is the defect coming back; the row below says which substance the numberless ones reach.

Restated 23 October 2026: a resource in the ground is now read as its element (`+ground-resource-is-element`), so the openLCA ground-resource rows of this name no longer reach the ion, and their flows in `Resource → Ground` are gone. The build records those two rows under the element's name, `Titanium`, so the name selects 24 of the 26.

expectations.title: A numberless `Titanium Ion` row reaches `Titanium, ion` by its name, and the merge says so
expectations.comment: The river row, one of the fourteen; `basis: label` because the name is all it ships. On the build of 20 October 2026 it minted the second `Titanium, ion`.

expectations.title: One substance is labelled `Titanium, ion`
expectations.comment: Two on the build of 20 October 2026, and the synonym withdrawn from both; one, carrying the standard's `Titanium Ion`, is what 0401 states as well.

expectations.title: openLCA's seven rows recorded as plain `Carbon dioxide` reach fossil carbon dioxide or biogenic uptake
expectations.comment: Names match case-insensitively, and the name the merge records is the enriched label, so `Carbon dioxide` selects GreenDelta's six title-cased `Carbon Dioxide` rows and ecoinvent's `Carbon dioxide, in air` (cc6a1abb), which the package ships under ecoinvent's uuid. Every method in the package scores GreenDelta's five air rows as fossil and its resource row as uptake, and `openlca-2.8.2-match-overrides.json` sends them to EF's fossil flows and biogenic uptake; cc6a1abb goes to biogenic uptake by override too, where ecoinvent's own copy goes (0435). Restated on 24 October 2026, keeping the id: the claim said eleven rows and three substances, and explained the other five as ecoinvent's carbon dioxide rows reaching carbon dioxide of unstated origin exactly as ecoinvent's do. They were not: four were ecoinvent's `Carbon dioxide, from soil or biomass stock`, whose ecoinvent copies reach land-use-change carbon dioxide, and the fifth was cc6a1abb, whose ecoinvent copy reaches biogenic uptake. On the build of 5802a4c the openLCA copies had lost the qualifier and created plain carbon dioxide flows; on the build of 34984fd the four from-soil rows reach land-use-change carbon dioxide and are recorded under their own name (#435). On the build of 20 October 2026 (merge run `76b3ec8f`) the six plain rows also reached carbon dioxide of unstated origin and minted its long-term air flow again (0914); the per-row claims below name each row's target.

expectations.title: The plain `Carbon dioxide` row in air, unspecified reaches fossil carbon dioxide
expectations.comment: One of the five; the other four are its siblings in rural, urban, long-term and cruise-height air, each with the fossil flow of its own compartment as target.

expectations.title: The plain `Carbon dioxide` row in high population density reaches fossil carbon dioxide
expectations.comment: GreenDelta's row in `Emission to air / high population density`, scored as fossil by every method in the package; its target is EF's fossil flow in urban air.

expectations.title: The plain `Carbon dioxide` row in low population density reaches fossil carbon dioxide
expectations.comment: GreenDelta's row in `Emission to air / low population density`, scored as fossil by every method in the package; its target is EF's fossil flow in rural air.

expectations.title: The plain `Carbon dioxide` row in low population density, long-term reaches fossil carbon dioxide
expectations.comment: GreenDelta's row in `Emission to air / low population density, long-term`, scored as fossil by every method in the package; its target is EF's fossil flow in long-term air.

expectations.title: The plain `Carbon dioxide` row in lower stratosphere + upper troposphere reaches fossil carbon dioxide
expectations.comment: GreenDelta's row in `Emission to air / lower stratosphere + upper troposphere`, scored as fossil by every method in the package; its target is EF's fossil flow in aircraft cruise height.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Carbon dioxide` resource row reaches biogenic uptake from air
expectations.comment: IPCC 2013 scores it as CO2 uptake; the target is the flow BAFU's `Carbon dioxide, in air` rows reach.

expectations.title: openLCA's three kilogram `Peat` rows reach the megajoule fuel, converted
expectations.comment: At the package's own 9.76 MJ/kg. On the build of 20 October 2026 the biotic row minted a kilogram flow in `Resource → Biotic` (0450, 0856). The biotic row is ecoinvent's under ecoinvent's uuid, and ecoinvent's own copy is placed on `Peat, Horticulture` by the current merge; the disagreement is recorded on #412 and left for a measurement of its own.

expectations.title: openLCA's eighteen `Hydrocarbons, unspecified` rows reach EF's bucket
expectations.comment: Two by EF's own uuid, sixteen by curated target. On the build of 20 October 2026 the sixteen minted `Hydrocarbons, Unspecified` (0825).

expectations.title: The only openLCA kilogram rows named for water are the three dissolved-element rows
expectations.comment: The 52 rows the package measures water by mass -- `Waste water`, `Water`, the 29 `Water, ...` names, `Thermally polluted water` and `Chemically polluted water` -- are rewritten to cubic metres before the merge reads them, so none arrives in kilograms; `0409-bafu-waste-water-is-published-in-cubic-metres` says the flows are cubic metres. Names match case-insensitively, and the three kilogram rows whose names still contain `water` are `Magnesium, 0.13% in water` (two rows) and `Bromine, 0.0023% in water`: an element dissolved in water, reaching magnesium and bromine by registry number, measured as the element in kilograms. The next claim pins them. On the six-list build of 20 October 2026 (merge run `0c16f168`) the count was five: the first fifty rewrites took the names beginning `Water` and `Waste water` and missed the two ending in `polluted water`.

expectations.title: The three kilogram rows named `… in water` are magnesium and bromine dissolved in water
expectations.comment: `Magnesium, 0.13% in water` in `Resource / in ground` and `Resource / in water`, and `Bromine, 0.0023% in water` in `Resource / in water`: the mass is the element's, and each reaches its element by registry number. Together with the previous claim this says every kilogram row named for water is one of these three.

expectations.title: The two `Waste water` rows measured by mass reach the cubic-metre flow
expectations.comment: The row in water, unspecified. On the build of 20 October 2026 it published a kilogram `Waste water` flow (0409) and its GreenDelta factor was a unit crossing.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Thermally polluted water` reaches the cubic-metre cooling-water flow as cooling water
expectations.comment: `water-flow-materials.json` reads the row as returned cooling water, warm rather than contaminated, and the merge placed it on the cubic-metre `Cooling water` flow in water, unspecified, from the first build; shipped in kilograms it was a unit crossing there (six-list build of 20 October 2026, merge run `0c16f168`).

expectations.title: openLCA's `Chemically polluted water` publishes contaminated water in cubic metres
expectations.comment: Read as contaminated water, as BAFU's row of the same name is. BAFU's is filed in a river, this one in water, unspecified, so it is the only row on its flow; on the six-list build of 20 October 2026 (merge run `0c16f168`) that flow was published in kilograms.

expectations.title: openLCA's `HG-02` reaches the hydrofluoropolyether EF renamed
expectations.comment: On the build of 20 October 2026 it minted a second substance named `HG-02` and `0571-hg-02-is-findable-again` lost the synonym.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Tribromomethane` reaches bromoform
expectations.comment: Twenty rows of the package named `Bromoform` carry 75-25-2 and reach it; this one carried no number.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Helium, in natural gas, in ground` reaches helium
expectations.comment: ecoinvent's row under ecoinvent's uuid, copied without its number.

expectations.title: The package's `Carbon` in the ground is published as elemental carbon's one ground resource
expectations.comment: Scored by the Crustal Scarcity Indicator alone, at 140: the element in the crust, which no other list inventories. Kept on purpose; 0915's claim that no such flow exists is restated to AGRIBALYSE's rows, which are soil carbon stock and go to EF's stock flow.

expectations.title: openLCA's two unqualified biomass-energy rows reach the `Biomass` flow the other lists reach

subject.name: Energy, Gross Calorific Value, In Biomass

expectations.comment: On the six-list build with the first corrections (merge run `0c16f168`) they minted a flow of their own, and the lookup sent BAFU's rows of the name to it.

expectations.title: openLCA's two `Anhydrite` rows reach the calcium sulfate the other lists' anhydrite reaches
expectations.comment: 14798-04-0 is the mineral's own number, which EF 3.1 does not carry; #597 reads anhydrite and calcium sulfate as one substance. On merge run `0c16f168` the two rows minted `Anhydrite` and the lookup sent ecoinvent 3.8's and AGRIBALYSE's rows to it (0597).

expectations.title: openLCA's `Propane, Dibromopentafluoro-` reaches the substance Stepwise's row of that name reaches
expectations.comment: Shipped under Stepwise's SimaPro spelling with no number; on merge run `0c16f168` it minted a substance of its own and the lookup sent Stepwise's row to it.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Propane, Dibromofluoro-` reaches the substance Stepwise's row of that name reaches
expectations.comment: Shipped under Stepwise's SimaPro spelling with no number; on merge run `0c16f168` it minted a substance of its own and the lookup sent Stepwise's row to it.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Propane, 1,3-dibromo-1,1,3,3-tetrafluoro-` reaches the substance Stepwise's row of that name reaches
expectations.comment: Shipped under Stepwise's SimaPro spelling with no number; on merge run `0c16f168` it minted a substance of its own and the lookup sent Stepwise's row to it.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Propane, 1,2,3-tribromo-3,3-difluoro-` reaches the substance Stepwise's row of that name reaches
expectations.comment: Shipped under Stepwise's SimaPro spelling with no number; on merge run `0c16f168` it minted a substance of its own and the lookup sent Stepwise's row to it.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Propane, 1,2,2-tribromo-3,3,3-trifluoro-` reaches the substance Stepwise's row of that name reaches
expectations.comment: Shipped under Stepwise's SimaPro spelling with no number; on merge run `0c16f168` it minted a substance of its own and the lookup sent Stepwise's row to it.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Ethane, Tribromofluoro-` reaches the substance Stepwise's row of that name reaches
expectations.comment: Shipped under Stepwise's SimaPro spelling with no number; on merge run `0c16f168` it minted a substance of its own and the lookup sent Stepwise's row to it.
